Scorching heat expected in much of Japan, says weather agency
By Xinhua
Scorching heat is expected to grip much of western and eastern Japan on Monday, the weather agency said, urging people to take extra caution against heatstroke.
Due to a high-pressure system, sweltering weather is expected in much of the country, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA), with a heatstroke alert in place for 31 prefectures, from Tokyo and Chiba in the Kanto region through Okinawa in southwestern Japan.
The JMA forecast daytime highs of 39 degrees Celsius in Hita city, Oita prefecture, and 38 C in cities including Saga, Yamaguchi and Nara.
The mercury is also forecast to jump in areas of Kumamoto prefecture that were hit hard by a massive earthquake in late July, with daytime highs to reach 38 C in Kumamoto city, 37 C in Amakusa city and 36 C in Hitoyoshi city.

Seoul back under heat wave warnings after 15-day break
Heat wave warnings have returned to parts of Seoul as sweltering days and tropical nights grip much of the country.
Children play in a fountain at Gwanghwamun Square in Jongno District, central Seoul, on Aug. 23.
NEWS1
The temperature in Seoul is rising again, with heat wave warnings reissued for parts of the capital Monday, 15 days after being downgraded to an advisory on Aug. 9.
Heat wave advisories were also upgraded to warnings in parts of Gyeonggi, Gangwon, South Chungcheong, North and South Gyeongsang and Busan.
The Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA) upgraded heat wave advisories to warnings for southeastern and northeastern Seoul as of 11 a.m. Monday. Advisories remain in effect for southwestern and northwestern Seoul.
The KMA divides heat wave alerts into three tiers based primarily on the daily maximum apparent temperature: advisories are issued when the apparent temperature is forecast to reach 33 degrees Celsius (91.4 degrees Fahrenheit) or higher for at least two consecutive days, warnings at 35 degrees Celsius or higher for at least two days and the most severe tier, a "heat wave critical warning," introduced this year, when the apparent temperature is forecast to reach 38 degrees Celsius or higher — or the actual temperature reaches 39 degrees Celsius or higher — for at least one day.
Areas where warnings were newly issued include Gimpo, Hanam and Gwangju in Gyeonggi; lowland and mountainous areas of Donghae and Samcheok in Gangwon; Gongju, Cheongyang County and Boryeong in South Chungcheong; Gumi, Yecheon County, northern Gimcheon and lowland areas of Uljin County in North Gyeongsang; Tongyeong and central Hamyang County in South Gyeongsang; and eastern Busan.
Tropical night advisories are also in effect for 84 areas nationwide, including southwestern Seoul. Seoul's lowest apparent temperature overnight was 27.7 degrees Celsius, with hot and humid conditions persisting through the night.
The nighttime heat is expected to continue for the time being, with morning lows forecast to remain above 25 degrees Celsius.

The final week of August will begin with moderately warm, pleasant summer weather, with daytime temperatures around 30°C and refreshing mornings. However, the heatwave will return in the second half of the week. Showers and thunderstorms may occur in several parts of Hungary on Tuesday, but most of the week is expected to be sunny and dry, according to a forecast from HungaroMet Zrt. sent to MTI on Sunday.
The beginning of the week
On Monday, cloudier areas will gradually clear and become more broken, followed by plenty of sunshine alongside high and developing cumulus clouds. The northern parts of the country may remain cloudier at times, with a chance of light rain or showers. Northerly winds may occasionally produce stronger gusts. Daytime temperatures will generally range from 26 to 32°C.
On Tuesday, cloud cover will increase significantly from the south-west and west. Showers and thunderstorms may occur in several parts of Transdanubia, with rain potentially spreading further east from the evening onwards. Southerly and south-easterly winds will occasionally strengthen in Transdanubia, while easterly and north-easterly winds will pick up elsewhere. Temperatures will rise from 9–19°C in the early morning to 26–33°C in the afternoon.
Wednesday and Thursday
By Wednesday morning, patches of fog and low cloud may form in western and south-western Hungary. Once these clear, sunny weather is expected across the country, with only a few cumulus and high clouds. A few showers may still occur in the morning, but no further rainfall is expected later in the day. Winds will generally remain moderate. Morning temperatures will range from 11 to 21°C, while afternoon highs will reach 27–32°C.
Thursday will be mostly clear and sunny, with only a few high and cumulus clouds and no rainfall expected. Winds will turn south-easterly and southerly and strengthen. Overnight lows will range from 9 to 19°C, while afternoon temperatures will reach 29–34°C.

The weekend
Friday is expected to be sunny with only a few clouds. No rain is expected during the day, although showers and thunderstorms may develop overnight in northern and north-western areas. South-westerly and southerly winds will strengthen across much of the country. Temperatures will range from 14–22°C in the morning to a scorching 32–38°C in the afternoon.
On Saturday, cloud cover will temporarily increase significantly, with scattered showers and thunderstorms likely. Winds will turn north-westerly and may become strong across large parts of the country. Early morning temperatures will range from 18 to 24°C, while afternoon highs will generally reach 28–34°C.
Sunday is expected to be mostly sunny, with no significant rainfall. North-westerly winds may bring occasional stronger gusts. Temperatures will range from 11–19°C in the morning to 25–30°C in the afternoon, according to HungaroMet (met.hu).

THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Isolated rain is likely to continue in Kerala, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issuing weather warnings until Tuesday, the day before Thiruvonam. No district has been issued a rain forecast for Thiruvonam.
A yellow alert has been issued for Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Kannur and Kasaragod districts today. Kottayam, Idukki and Ernakulam will be under a yellow alert tomorrow. Fishing has been banned along the Kerala, Karnataka and Lakshadweep coasts today.
Due to the possibility of the Kallakkadal phenomenon, coastal areas from Thiruvananthapuram to Thrissur are likely to experience high waves and sea incursions until 11.30 pm today.
